claims.subject: ceramic_production
claims.value: Japanese porcelain production developed in Hizen/Arita in the early seventeenth century; early Imari commonly used cobalt blue under a transparent glaze on a white ground.
claims.confidence_reason: Supported by cited museum/heritage/specialist evidence at the stated scope.
claims.interpretation: Use Hizen/Arita context for Edo blue-and-white porcelain instead of importing Chinese Ming manufacturing identity wholesale.
prompt_implications: For an Edo blue-and-white artifact, use Arita/Hizen porcelain logic: cobalt underglaze, clear glaze, kiln-fired white porcelain body, and period-appropriate Japanese decorative handling.

claims.subject: print_process
claims.value: Edo ukiyo-e woodblock prints were collaborative products involving designer, engraver/carver, printer, and publisher.
claims.confidence_reason: Supported by cited museum/heritage/specialist evidence at the stated scope.
claims.interpretation: The visible image should behave like a print made through carved blocks and registered color impressions, not like a digital painting with an “ukiyo-e” label.
prompt_implications: Use carved keyline logic, separate color impressions, registration-aware edges, absorbent paper, and hand-printed tonal variation.

claims.subject: print_material
claims.value: Cherry wood blocks, separate color blocks, registration guides, mulberry paper, and baren printing are historically grounded production anchors for Edo color woodblock printing.
claims.confidence_reason: Supported by cited museum/heritage/specialist evidence at the stated scope.
claims.interpretation: Use these as causal material cues, not decorative jargon.
prompt_implications: Let contours show carved-line discipline; let colors read as layered hand-printed impressions with subtle registration/pressure variation and paper absorption.

claims.subject: medium_boundary
claims.value: Edo blue-and-white porcelain and ukiyo-e are distinct production systems even when they share period or motifs.
claims.confidence_reason: Supported by cited museum/heritage/specialist evidence at the stated scope.
claims.interpretation: Shared Edo context does not justify importing woodblock paper texture, carved keylines, or registration artifacts onto glazed porcelain unless explicitly requested as a hybrid.
prompt_implications: For ceramic transformation, express brush-painted cobalt under clear glaze following the curved vessel surface; do not add paper fibers, key-block outlines, or print-registration artifacts.
